mostWorthwhile.text: Following fallen wood through fungal decomposition to renewed forest growth made the nutrient cycle concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial rainfall-and-air combination was the least engaging: it was the only choice, and its connection to forest renewal was not yet clear.

surprise.text: Forest transpiration contributing to rainfall far downwind was an interesting connection I hadn't expected from the decomposition goal.

arbitrary.text: Rainfall plus air initially seemed disconnected from the goals, although the resulting storm explained how dead wood could reach the forest floor.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the contrast between decomposition and peat preservation, and the forest-rain connection, made the chapter's ideas worth exploring. The limited choices made it more guided than a discovery puzzle, though.
